text:
The unemployment rate is 6.2% and falling, payrolls are averaging about 245k a month, and the fed funds rate is 0.09%. That points to mid-2014. Headline CPI at 2.0% and a 10-year yield of 2.34% fit the same period.

The 12-month equity return of 24.7% with the market at its high also fits. The 10-year yield fell about 14bp over 3 months, from roughly 2.5% to 2.34%. In July 2014 unemployment was 6.2% and the 10-year yield was about 2.5%. In June 2014 unemployment was 6.1%, though it was 6.3% as first published, and the 10-year yield was 2.53%. In August 2014 the 10-year yield was 2.34% and unemployment was 6.1%. Later revisions complicate the unemployment comparison.

The 1-month return of +3.9% for US equities matches August 2014, when the S&P rose about 3.9%. The 20y+ Treasury return of +4.7% also fits August. The data as first published showed unemployment of 6.2% for July, which was still the latest reading at end-August (the August report came out in September). So the snapshot is August 2014.
